2027-05-05.title: Sixth Wednesday of Resurrection
2027-05-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Be imitators of God, as beloved children
2027-05-05.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost. Tomorrow, Thursday 6 May, is the feast of the Ascension of our Lord, a day of obligation; the evening prayer of today already belongs to the feast in many parishes (verify locally).
2027-05-05.verse: “This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.”
theo: On the eve of the Ascension the Church gives us words from the Last Supper, words of a friend who is about to go away. “I have said these things to you so that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be complete.” Jesus speaks of joy at the very hour when he is about to suffer. His joy is not the absence of trouble; it is the joy of the Son who knows himself loved by the Father and who loves to the end. He wants that joy in us, and he tells us where it is found: “This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.” The measure is not our feelings or our convenience but his own love: “No one has greater love than this, to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.” Tomorrow we will see him go up into heaven. Before he goes, he reminds us that the proof of his love was the Cross, and that the only way to remain in his joy is to love in the same way.

Then comes a word that every Christian should hear as addressed to himself: “I do not call you servants any longer, because the servant does not know what the master is doing; but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I have heard from my Father.” In the Old Testament only a few were called friends of God: Abraham (Isaiah 41:8; James 2:23) and Moses, with whom the Lord spoke “face to face, as one speaks to a friend” (Exodus 33:11). Now Jesus gives that name to fishermen and tax collectors, and through them to us. And he adds: “You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last”. Friendship with Christ is not a private consolation; it sends us out. The disciples would understand this after the Ascension and Pentecost, when the friends of Jesus became his witnesses to the ends of the earth. It is worth asking, on this eve: do I relate to Christ as a slave who obeys from fear, or as a friend who knows the Master's heart and shares his work?

Paul's letter to the Ephesians draws the practical conclusion: “Therefore be imitators of God, as beloved children, and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.” Children imitate the parents they love; beloved children of God learn to love as he loves. Then Paul becomes very concrete. Sexual impurity and greed “must not even be mentioned among you, as is proper among saints”, and “Entirely out of place is obscene, silly, and vulgar talk; but instead, let there be thanksgiving.” In our time much obscene and vulgar talk passes through the screens in our hands, in jokes forwarded in groups and in what is watched in secret. Paul's remedy is not only a list of things to avoid but a positive habit: thanksgiving. A heart that thanks God is slow to soil itself. Greed, Paul adds, is a form of idolatry, the worship of things in place of God. On the eve of the Ascension we lift our eyes to the One who goes up to the Father, and we let him lift our hearts from what is low to what lasts: love, purity and gratitude.
outline: The eve of the Ascension: the words of a friend about to go away.
Point 1 · That your joy may be complete
Love one another as I have loved you.
Point 2 · I have called you friends
Chosen and sent to bear fruit that will last.
“This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.”
live: Do one hidden act of self-giving love today for someone who cannot repay you.
Spend ten minutes tonight speaking to Jesus as a friend, telling him about your day.
Delete or refuse to forward one unworthy message today, and thank God for three gifts instead.
fathers: Here we are, you and I, and I hope that Christ is the third among us. Friendship that begins in Christ, grows according to Christ and is perfected in Christ is a stairway to the friendship of God.
Blessed is the one who loves you, Lord, and his friend in you, and his enemy for your sake. Such a one never loses anyone dear to him, for all are dear in the One who is never lost.
magis: Jesus makes charity the new commandment: by loving his own to the end, he shows the Father's love which he receives, and by loving one another the disciples imitate the love of Jesus.
The virtue of chastity blossoms in friendship; it shows the disciple how to follow and imitate him who has chosen us as his friends.
Thanksgiving characterises the prayer of the Church, which in celebrating the Eucharist reveals and becomes more fully what she is.
2027-05-05.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, on the eve of your Ascension you call us your friends and give us your commandment of love. Let your joy be in us and make our joy complete. Teach us to love as you have loved us, to the laying down of our lives. Keep our hearts and our words clean, and fill our mouths with thanksgiving. You chose us: send us to bear fruit that will last, and tomorrow lift our hearts with you to the Father. Amen. Alleluia!
altar: The Holy Qurbana is the fragrant offering of which Paul speaks: Christ who loved us and gave himself up for us. Here the Friend lays down his life and gives it to us as food, so that we may love one another as he has loved us.

quick: Jesus wants his joy in us; it is found in loving as he loved.
I have called you friends; I chose you to bear fruit that will last.
Paul: be imitators of God; instead of vulgar talk, let there be thanksgiving.
2027-05-05.action: Do one hidden act of self-giving love today, and thank God for three gifts before you sleep.
2027-05-05.question: Do I relate to Jesus as a fearful servant or as a friend who shares his heart and his work?

family.explain: Jesus said to his disciples, ‘You are my friends.’ He also says it to us! A good friend shares secrets, helps when things are hard, and is happy when we are happy. Jesus is that kind of friend. He even gave his life for us. He asks us to love each other the way he loves us.
family.intention: We pray for our friends, and for children who have no friends.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be a good friend to someone this week, the way Jesus is a friend to us?”

illus: A teacher at a school in Changanassery noticed that a new boy from another state ate his lunch alone every day. She did not lecture the class. She simply asked one of her students, a quiet girl, to sit with the new boy and help him with Malayalam. Within a month there was a small group at that lunch table. At the end of the year the boy wrote in a card, ‘In this school I found friends.’ The girl later said that she had only tried to do what Jesus did when he called ordinary people his friends.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us your friends. As we gather in your name, let your joy be in us and teach us to love one another as you have loved us. Amen. Alleluia!
share: So that my joy may be in you (John 15:11). Where do I find true joy?
Love one another as I have loved you (John 15:12). Whom do I find it hard to love?
I have called you friends (John 15:15). How is my friendship with Jesus?
Let there be thanksgiving (Ephesians 5:4). What can I thank God for today?
pm.resp: Jesus, our friend, teach us to love.
interc: For the Church, that she may be known by the love of her members for one another.
For young people, that they may keep their hearts and words clean and find true friends.
For those who are lonely, especially migrants and the elderly, that they may find friendship.
For families, that thanksgiving may fill our homes in place of quarrelling.
For all of us, that we may prepare our hearts for the feast of the Ascension tomorrow.
pm.close: Father, your Son has called us friends and chosen us to bear fruit that will last. Make us imitators of you, as beloved children, living in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, tomorrow is the Ascension. Today Jesus speaks to us like a friend who is going away: “I have said these things to you so that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be complete” (John 15:11).
He gives us one commandment: “love one another as I have loved you” (John 15:12). How did he love us? “No one has greater love than this, to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.”
Then he says something wonderful: “I have called you friends” (John 15:15). Not servants, but friends. And he chose us to go and bear fruit that will last.
Paul tells us to be “imitators of God, as beloved children” (Ephesians 5:1). That means living in love, keeping our hearts and words pure, and instead of vulgar talk, giving thanks.
Tonight, let us speak to Jesus as a friend, and tomorrow come to the Holy Qurbana to celebrate his Ascension with joy. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus calls you his friend! A friend shares, helps and loves.
Tomorrow Jesus goes up to heaven, but he is still our friend. Talk to him tonight before you sleep.

intro: Theme: “This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.”
On the eve of the Ascension: the joy of Jesus, the friendship he offers, and the call to imitate God in love, purity and thanksgiving.

sub: Live in love as Christ loved us.
q: You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy.
Therefore be imitators of God, as beloved children, and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us
points.apply: Choose one way this week to love as Christ loved: patiently, humbly, at a cost.

sub: Friends who know the Master's heart.
q: But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham, my friend
but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I have heard from my Father.
points.apply: Spend some minutes each evening this week speaking to Jesus as to a friend.

sub: Thanksgiving in place of vulgar talk.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last
points.apply: Replace one habit of careless or unclean talk with a habit of thanksgiving.

concl: Before he ascends, Jesus calls us friends and sends us to love as he loved.
Let us imitate God as beloved children and bear fruit that will last.
2027-05-05.resolve: This week, do a hidden act of love each day, speak to Jesus as a friend each evening, and thank God for three gifts before sleeping.
